Operator: Good day, and welcome to the Vertex Capital Management Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. As a reminder, the instructions for joining the question and answer session are available by pressing the star key followed by one on your telephone keypad. Please be advised that today's conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson: Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Vertex Capital Management's Q3 2024 results. Joining me on today's call are Michael Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; David Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Investment Officer; Tom Hargrove, Head of Distribution; Emily Wong, Head of Operations; Robert Kline, Head of Risk Management; and Anna Petrov, Head of Technology.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that some of the statements made today may be forward-looking. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Michael Reynolds.

Michael Reynolds: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. I'm pleased to report on our performance for Q3 2024. We achieved solid results this quarter, driven by robust organic growth and continued market share gains across key asset classes and channels. Our AUM grew to $1.8 trillion.

David Chen: Thank you, Michael. From a financial perspective, Vertex Capital Management delivered strong results in Q3 2024. Our revenue was $520 million, representing a 15% increase year-over-year. This growth was primarily driven by higher average AUM, favorable product mix shifts toward higher-margin alternatives, and performance fees from realizations in private markets. Our expenses were $340 million, resulting in net income of $120 million. Our expense ratio improved due to operational leverage, technology efficiencies, and disciplined cost management.

Let me provide more detail on our capital allocation strategy, which remains central to delivering superior total shareholder returns in this evolving asset management environment. With $1.8 trillion in AUM as of quarter-end and fee-related earnings of $1.2 billion year-to-date, we maintain a strong balance sheet featuring $4.5 billion in cash and equivalents and a net debt-to-EBITDA ratio of 0.8x. This financial flexibility allows us to execute across our four-pillar framework: shareholder returns, organic growth investments, inorganic M&A opportunities, and opportunistic initiatives.

Shareholder returns have been our top priority, absorbing 55% of free cash flow over the past 12 months. We adhere to a progressive dividend policy targeting 40-45% of adjusted fee-related earnings. In Q3, we declared a quarterly dividend of $0.65 per share, up 8% year-over-year, yielding about 2.8% based on current prices—above the peer average of 2.1%. Our $3 billion share repurchase program, launched in February, has deployed $1.1 billion year-to-date, retiring 4.2% of shares at an average of $185, implying a 12.5% ROIC. We've timed buys opportunistically during August VIX spikes when the index averaged 22, pausing in October as markets stabilized, with 65% of the authorization remaining for potential acceleration on 10-15% drawdowns in tech or financials.

For organic growth investments, we've committed 25% of capital—around $450 million last year—to high-return projects scaling AUM and margins. Digital transformation is key, with $180 million into VertexOne, our AI-powered risk analytics platform tailored for multi-asset active management, cutting portfolio construction time 35% for $450 billion in active equities and lifting client retention to 95%. In alternatives, $120 million expanded our private credit business, now at $150 billion AUM with 22% YoY growth, capturing 7-9% yield premiums over public high-yield amid 5.25-5.50% Fed funds. North America drove 12% organic inflows via retirement channels into target-date funds; EMEA saw 15% growth in SFDR-compliant ESG despite regs; APAC added 9% through our $80 billion Hong Kong ETF suite, aided by China stimulus and Japan NISA.

On inorganic growth, 15% of capital—or $270 million—went to bolt-on M&A enhancing products and distribution. The Q2 QuantForge Advisors acquisition, a $25 billion multi-strat specialist, is delivering 200bps margin accretion via data synergies, akin to T. Rowe Price's quant push or State Street's ETFs. Our pipeline targets 8-10% IRR, focusing passive and alts, including advanced talks for a European UCITS ETF platform amid the $2 trillion passive shift—ETFs now 45% of our $600 billion beta business. LatAm private markets are next, eyeing Brazil pension reforms for 20%+ CAGR.

Our 20% opportunistic bucket holds $2.8 billion dry powder for dislocations, like seed capital in tokenization and crypto ETPs post-Bitcoin ETF approvals—our $5 billion product yields 50bps. We stress-test for 200bps rate hikes, with 150% liquidity coverage.

This dynamic approach targets 12-15% ROIC, outpacing Vanguard's low-cost or Blackstone's alts models. Amid deglobalization and AI capex, recurring fees are 92% of revenue; if AUM hits $2 trillion on 7% organic growth, we eye $2.5 billion shareholder returns in FY24, pivoting on macro—easing favors buybacks, volatility M&A. This drove 18% three-year TSR, beating KBW by 500bps.

Turning to organic growth and market share, for full-year 2023 we hit 12.4% organic AUM growth to $1.45 trillion from $1.28 trillion, excluding $85 billion from Horizon Alternatives acquisition. This split 6.2% market appreciation—active equities at 14.2% net, beating MSCI World by 320bps—and 6.2% net flows of $79.3 billion. Q4 accelerated to 4.1% on $22.4 billion inflows into fixed income and ETFs. We outpaced peers' 3.8% per Morningstar, capturing 45bps industry flows.

By asset class: Equities (52%) grew 15.7% organically with $42.1 billion inflows; Vertex Global Growth Fund drew $18.9 billion institutionally, gaining 120bps U.S. large-cap growth share; VESG ETF $9.2 billion. Fixed income (28%) 9.3% on $24.6 billion, top-decile VCBX clawing 65bps from PIMCO/Vanguard. Alts/multi-asset (15%) 8.9% with $12.5 billion, private credit $7.8 billion. Cash flat at 0.2%.

Channels: Institutional (55%) $48.2 billion (7.1%); wealth/retail (30%) $22.6 billion (9.8%) via Vertex Digital Portfolios at $15 billion; intermediary $8.5 billion. Regions: NA 13.2%, EMEA 10.8% ($19.4 billion UCITS), APAC 14.5% ($12.1 billion, top-5 active equities).

Vertex Alpha GenAI boosted flows 22%; direct indexing $4.7 billion seed; ESG $320 billion up 18.2%. Our active alpha thesis gains in 12-15% CAGR segments; 92% retention, $145 billion RFPs position us well.

On operating margin trends, full-year 2023 hit 32.4%, up 210bps from 30.3%, best since pre-pandemic. Q4 33.8% beat Q3 32.1%, 400bps two-year stack outpacing T. Rowe/Invesco mid-20s.

Revenue from $1.2 trillion average AUM up 12%, $85 billion inflows; ETFs 28% AUM at 22bps fees; perf fees $450 million up 25%. Blended fee 42bps stable, alts 85bps offsetting mutual fund de-emphasis.

Expenses up 8% to $3.8 billion vs. 11% revenue growth. Comp/benefits (52%) up 6% on flows/performance, $120 million deferred clawbacks. Non-comp up 10%, offset by $75 million shared services, flat marketing % via digital (40% retail).

$250 million platform modernization: GAP Nexus automated 65% ops, 15% unit costs down; AI cut research 20%; blockchain custody pilot 30% reconciliation savings.

Regions: Americas 35%, EMEA 30% up (UCITS), APAC 25% countering fee wars with alts. Outlook: 34-36% 2024 on 8-10% AUM, alts to 25%, genAI opex cut, 70% FCF returns.

Operating expenses totaled $248.7 million in Q2 equivalent context, up 4.2% YoY but flat sequentially on $452 billion average AUM up 12%. OER 21.6bps vs. 24.8bps, competitive with BlackRock 22bps.

Comp/benefits $142.3 million (57.2%) up 6.1% on incentives/headcount to 2,450, quants added. Tech/data $42.1 million (16.9%) up 15% on AWS/VertexOne/AI pilots. Distribution/marketing $31.5 million (12.7%) down 2.8% via digital. G&A $22.4 million (9%) up 3% audits/cyber. Other $10.4 million down 12%.

YTD 70bps OER compression; automation 18% back-office cuts. Sub-20bps 2025 via AI, alts mix, fintech.

AUM hit $1.45 trillion Q3 record, 12% YoY/4.2% QoQ, beating peers' 9%. $28 billion organic, $42 billion markets, $3 billion FX, -$15 billion outflows.

Breakdown: Equities 48% $696B +6.1% QoQ/+18% YoY (tech/ETFs); FI 28% $406B +1.8%/+7% (short-duration); Alts 16% $232B +4.9%/+22% (private credit); Cash 6% $87B +2.3%; Multi 2% $29B +3.5%.

Strategic: Innovation (AI/ESG ETFs $2.5B), PinnacleFlow retention +15%, APAC 18%.

Lisa Patel: Thank you, David. On the investment front, we continue to focus on delivering strong risk-adjusted returns for our clients. Our key strategies performed well, particularly in equities. We are navigating the current market environment by emphasizing quality factors and selective duration plays. We launched Vertex AI Equity ETF this quarter, and the early reception has been positive, with $3 billion in inflows and strong outperformance.

Our fund performance relative to peers and benchmarks validates our research-driven active approach across $1.8 trillion AUM. Core equities (55%): Large-Cap Growth 8.2% Q3 beat Russell 1000 Growth 210bps, peers 320bps; TTM 28.4% vs. 25.1%/23.7%; 3yr 11.2% vs. 9.8%/8.5%. Stock picks NVIDIA/Lilly, underweight cyclicals. SMID 6.8% beat Russell 2000 Growth 150bps.

FI: Total Return 2.1% beat Agg 40bps, peers 60bps; HY 4.3% beat ICE 90bps. Alts: Macro Hedge 5.6% beat HFRI 220bps; PE interval 12.4% annualized DPI 1.18x.

Regions: NA 65% alpha, EMEA EM Europe, APAC underweight China. Dispersion favors actives (62% beat 10yr); AI signals +15% accuracy. Outcomes products $2.5B inflows. Forward: Quality tilt, alts dry powder.

Tom Hargrove: Thank you, Lisa. From a distribution perspective, we saw strong inflows into our ETF funds. Our efforts to expand our reach in EMEA and APAC are paying off, as evidenced by key partnerships.

Net flows totaled $18.2 billion Q2-like, strongest since Q4 2022, YTD $32.8 billion (4.2% AUM), ahead peers 2-3%. Institutional 55% $10B (pension $2.8B, ESG $1.5B); NA $6.2B, EMEA LDI $45B, APAC SWFs. Retail 30% $5.5B (ETFs $3.3B APEX $2.1B); US $4.2B, Europe UCITS. Alts 15% $2.7B (credit $1.2B); US $1.6B.

On partnerships: Schwab SMA $4.2B ($12.8B total); Morgan Stanley E*TRADE $2.9B ETF; LPL IBD $3.1B alts; Natixis UCITS €5.2B. Models 31% AUM $6.7B Envestnet; robo $1.8B. Regions: Americas 22%, LatAm 41%, EMEA 28%, APAC 37% HK ETF $4.3B. Channel 360 $150M tech.

Emily Wong: Thank you, Tom. Operationally, we've made significant progress in streamlining our middle and back office functions. This has resulted in increased efficiency and reduced operational risk, with RPA automating 18% of processes and hybrid models saving 15% on occupancy. We are also focused on outsourcing data to AWS/BNP for $50 million savings and blockchain custody pilots targeting 30% reductions.

Robert Kline: Thank you, Emily. From a risk management perspective, we continue to maintain a robust framework to identify, assess, and mitigate risks across the organization. We have enhanced our monitoring of market volatility and liquidity risks and are taking steps to address potential vulnerabilities. This includes VertexOne AI for real-time stress-testing, 150% liquidity coverage, and hedging duration in FI amid higher-for-longer rates.

Anna Petrov: Thank you, Robert. On the technology front, we are investing in advanced analytics and AI to enhance our investment decision-making process and improve client service. We are also focused on strengthening our cybersecurity posture with $2.5 million hardening. Specifically, Vertex Alpha GenAI boosts flow conversion 22%, GAP Nexus automates 65%, and API gateways slash onboarding to 48 hours.

Michael Reynolds: In summary, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering value to our shareholders. We are focused on executing our strategic priorities and capitalizing on the opportunities ahead. This includes scaling alternatives to 25% AUM, tech-led efficiencies for margin expansion, and diversified flows positioning for 12-15% growth.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. As a reminder, to ask a question, please press star one on your telephone keypad. Our first question comes from Alex Rivera with Morningstar.

Alex Rivera: Good morning. Can you provide more details on trends in your operating margins?

David Chen: Good morning, Alex. As I noted, our full-year 2023 margins reached 32.4%, up 210bps, with Q4 at 33.8%. This leverages revenue growth from inflows and mix, stable 42bps fees, and opex discipline—comp tied to performance, tech automation via GAP Nexus saving 15% unit costs. Outlook 34-36% in 2024 on alts growth and AI opex cuts, outpacing peers.

Alex Rivera: Thank you. And a follow-up on your capital allocation priorities?

David Chen: Sure. Shareholder returns lead at 55% FCF—dividend up 8%, $1.1B buybacks at 12.5% ROIC. Organic 25% into VertexOne/private credit; M&A 15% like QuantForge 200bps accretion; opportunistic 20% for crypto/dislocations. Targets 12-15% ROIC, $2.5B returns FY24.

Operator: Our next question comes from Jordan Lee with Goldman Sachs.

Jordan Lee: Good morning. Could you elaborate on the performance of your equity funds?

Lisa Patel: Good morning, Jordan. Equities shone: Large-Cap Growth 8.2% Q3 +210bps Russell, +320bps peers; SMID 6.8% +150bps. Attribution from tech/healthcare picks like NVIDIA, quality tilts Sharpe 1.05. 62% beat benchmarks 10yr, AI signals enhancing.

Jordan Lee: And how is the new Vertex AI Equity ETF performing relative to expectations?

Tom Hargrove: Exceeding, Jordan. $3B inflows on 450bps S&P outperformance YTD, quant factors. Mirrors Schwab/LPL traction, active edge in ETF shift.

Operator: Our next question comes from Maria Gonzalez with Barclays.

Maria Gonzalez: Can you provide more color on the operational efficiencies you've gained?

Emily Wong: Absolutely, Maria. Streamlining middle/back office via GAP Nexus automated 65%, RPA 18% cuts; outsourcing AWS/BNP $50M savings; hybrid 15% occupancy. OER to 21.6bps, targeting sub-20bps.

Operator: Our next question comes from Kevin Patel with JPMorgan.

Kevin Patel: What are your thoughts on the current regulatory environment and its impact on your risk profile?

Robert Kline: Engaged proactively, Kevin. SFDR/MiFID II boosts ESG flows, but custody costs monitored; SEC T+1/Basel IV potential 50-100bps pressure mitigated by VertexOne stress-tests, 150% liquidity, FX hedges on 35% non-US.

Operator: Our next question comes from Samantha Kim with Fidelity.

Samantha Kim: How are you leveraging technology to improve investment performance?

Anna Petrov: Key focus, Samantha. Vertex Alpha GenAI +15% prediction accuracy via alt data/sentiment; VertexOne 35% faster construction; API real-time rebalancing 120bps tax alpha. Pilots blockchain custody, SOC2 compliance scaling models/SMAs.

Operator: Thank you. There are no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the call back over to Michael Reynolds for closing remarks.

Michael Reynolds: Thank you for joining us today. We appreciate your interest in Vertex Capital Management. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
